Job Description Summary:

Founded in 1824, the GW School of Medicine and Health Sciences ( SMHS ) is the 11th oldest medical school in the country and the first in the nation’s capital. Since its establishment, the school has been at the forefront of medical education, and has grown to include highly-ranked programs in the health and biomedical sciences. With dozens of top-tier residency programs, SMHS is a competitive and esteemed destination for medical school graduates across the country. Find out more here: http://smhs.gwu.edu/

The Department of Pharmacology and Physiology at The George Washington University School of Medicine and Health Sciences invites applications for a Senior Research Assistant position focused on examining the pharmacodynamics of oxytocin and different long-lasting oxytocin formulations in cell culture and in-vivo preparations.

The research in the Mendelowitz lab is focused on the parasympathetic control of the heart, how cardioprotective parasympathetic activity becomes diminished in many diseases with the goal of identifying targets to restore cardiac vagal activity and alleviate the risks and incidence of cardiovascular diseases. Atoms builds Physical AI— real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive.

This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across hardware, software, AI, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale.

We are roboticists, engineers, operators, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life.

If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us.

About The Role

The QC Technician is the last check between our electronics and the field. You will flash firmware onto circuit boards every day, run functional tests, and make sure every board that leaves the bench is correctly programmed, traceable, and working.

This is a hands-on, bench-based role on the hardware production team. You will work closely with hardware and firmware engineers, follow documented procedures, and flag anything that looks off before it reaches a vehicle.

What You'll Do

Flash bootloaders, firmware, and configuration files onto PCBs and modules using programming fixtures, JTAG/SWD debuggers, USB/serial tools, and in-house scripts.
Confirm the correct firmware version and configuration is loaded on every board, matched to the build order, and run batch flashing efficiently while keeping error rates near zero.
Run functional and power-on tests after flashing, following test procedures and checklists; visually inspect boards for physical defects such as damaged components, solder issues, bent pins, and connector damage.
Use multimeters, power supplies, and basic test equipment to check voltages and continuity.
Separate passing and failing units, and tag failures clearly for engineering review. Write clear failure reports with symptoms, steps taken, and photos where useful.
Log serial numbers, firmware versions, test results, and failures in our tracking system or spreadsheets, label boards and keep inventory of programmed, tested, and failed units accurate.
Do first-level troubleshooting on failed flashes and tests: re-seat connections, check cables, retry, and swap fixtures–escalate recurring or unexplained failures to hardware and firmware engineers with enough detail to act on.
Follow ESD-safe handling and keep the bench, fixtures, and tools clean, calibrated, and organized, suggest improvements to procedures, fixtures, and scripts that cut cycle time or errors.
Help keep work instructions and checklists up to date as firmware and hardware change, and support new product introductions and engineering builds when needed.

What We're Looking For

High school diploma or equivalent; technical certificate or associate degree in electronics or a related field is a plus.
3+ year of hands-on experience in electronics manufacturing, test, QC, or a similar bench role.
Comfortable handling PCBs and small components with ESD-safe practices.
Basic use of a multimeter and bench power supply.
Comfortable on a linux computer: running programs or scripts from instructions, using a command line at an intermediate level, and entering data accurately in spreadsheets or tracking tools.
Able to follow written procedures exactly and recognize when something doesn't match them, clear written and verbal communication for logging results and reporting failures.
Reliable, consistent, and comfortable with repetitive, high-volume work.
Background in automotive, robotics, or heavy equipment electronics preferred.
IPC-A-610 or IPC J-STD-001 certification, or working knowledge of PCB workmanship standards preferred.
Experience flashing microcontrollers (STM32, ESP32, NXP, or similar) with tools such as ST-Link, J-Link, or OpenOCD preferred.
Familiarity with Linux and running Python or shell scripts preferred.
Experience with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, or serial terminals (UART, CAN), basic soldering and rework skills, and experience with test fixtures, bed-of-nails testers, or production test stations preferred.

Physical Requirements

Bench work in a lab or production environment, standing or seated for long periods.
Lift and move boxes and equipment up to 25 lb.
Close-up visual work with small components; magnification provided.
Use of ESD protective equipment required.

jobs.description:
WHAT MAKES US A GREAT PLACE TO WORK

We are proud to be consistently recognized as one of the world’s best places to work. We are currently the top ranked consulting firm on Glassdoor Best Place to Work list and have earned the #1 overall spot a record seven times.
Extraordinary teams are at the heart of our business strategy, but these don’t happen by chance. They require intentional focus on bringing together a broad set of backgrounds, cultures, experiences, perspectives, and skills in a supportive and inclusive work environment. We hire people with exceptional talent and create an environment in which every individual can thrive professionally and personally.

WHO YOU'LL WORK WITH

About the Commercial Excellence practice

Bain's B2B Commercial Excellence practice works with clients to develop a clear go-to-market (GTM) strategy: building an in-depth understanding of market opportunity, designing effective sales coverage and capacity models to attack that opportunity, and creating an industrialized sales execution capability to ensure commercial success. Coro's software and data solutions are an innovative and increasingly critical part of this approach. To learn more about Coro, visit https://www.coro.io/
.

WHERE YOU'LL FIT WITHIN THE TEAM

About Coro
℠

The Coro ℠  business unit brings together Bain's proprietary suite of software-as-a-service (SaaS) and data-as-a-service (DaaS) tools, including cloud-based software, online capability assessments, and advanced analytics, focused on enabling Commercial Excellence for B2B companies.

The Impact You'll Have

Bain's Commercial Excellence work helps B2B companies turn market opportunity into booked revenue, through sharper go-to-market strategy, better sales coverage and capacity, and industrialized execution. The analytics underneath that work are what make it credible, and they are what you will own.
We are hiring an Expert Senior Manager, Data Science, to lead data science delivery and methodology across Coro's product suite. You will set the analytical approach on our most complex client engagements, lead the teams that deliver them, and make the calls on modeling design, validation, and where a bespoke analysis should become a productized capability. This is a senior, client-facing role: you will work directly with Bain partners and client executives, and you will be the person expected to defend the methodology in the room.
These capabilities power Coro's product suite, such as MoneyMap®, which builds a granular, bottoms-up view of market opportunity, and the repeatable analytics workflows behind Bain's B2B go-to-market work, across challenges such as opportunity mapping, indirect channel growth, and profitability analysis. The work spans propensity and predictive scoring, TAM and market sizing, entity resolution and data matching across third-party sources, and GenAI-driven classification and enrichment at scale. The role also includes ownership of the analytics and delivery of our pricing products, including ProfitCube.
You will also help build the capability itself, through recruiting, coaching, and raising the standard of how the team works, in keeping with Bain's apprenticeship model. You will have opportunities to work with major AI ecosystem partners through Bain's partnerships, collaborating on real client deployments and helping shape how emerging capabilities are applied in commercial settings.

As a senior member of the Coro data science team, you will:
Lead the delivery of Coro data science solutions across multiple concurrent client engagements, owning scope, methodology, quality and pace, and stepping in personally where the analytical problem warrants it
Collaborate closely with and influence Bain case teams, partners and senior client executives, framing commercial problems and translating them into analytical approaches and clear business recommendations
Develop and deploy production machine learning and analytical models that drive Coro solutions, including propensity and predictive scoring, TAM and market opportunity sizing, customer segmentation, entity resolution and data matching, and enrichment pipelines built on third-party data sources
Own the analytics and delivery of Coro's pricing products, including ProfitCube
Own the technical direction for GenAI-enabled analytical workflows, including LLM-based classification, enrichment and validation, and set the standards the team applies to prompt design, evaluation and output quality assurance
Develop Coro intellectual property and identify new opportunities for data science to extend the product suite, ensuring that repeatable analyses become re-usable frameworks, models and components rather than one-off case work
Work with Coro product managers and practice leadership to shape the roadmap, prioritize analytical features, and design the optimal approach to product delivery
Act as an expert advisor in proposal, pre-sales and pitch discussions, scoping the analytical approach, sizing the work, and supporting commercial conversations with clients
Lead and develop on-shore and off-shore delivery teams, providing coaching on problem-solving, work planning and data science techniques, and engaging constructively in the mutual feedback process
Keep abreast of new and current data science techniques and technologies, and assess where they create real advantage for our clients and our products
Share learnings and drive adoption of best demonstrated practices across the Coro and wider data science community, and work together to create a great working environment that attracts other great data scientists
Lead recruiting and onboarding of team members as needed, and identify opportunities to support the growth and scaling of the Coro business unit

This role requires a minimum of three days per week working together in person, either at a client location or at your Bain home office.  Willingness to travel to client locations (expected 20-40%, potential peak of 60%).

Advanced degree in a quantitative discipline such as Computer Science, Engineering, Econometrics, Statistics or Information Sciences such as business analytics or informatics
8-10 years of experience in analytics
3+ years of experience managing data scientists
Shipped production, enterprise scale data products
Track record of leading and collaborating on strategic initiatives, and of owning client relationships or workstreams end to end
Experience in B2B commercial or go-to-market analytics
Strong interpersonal and communication skills, including the ability to explain and discuss mathematical and machine learning technicalities with colleagues and clients from other disciplines
Solid fundamental knowledge of supervised and unsupervised machine learning algorithms such as classifiers, cluster analysis, dimension reduction, regression, sequence modeling, NLP/NLU, word and document embeddings, self-attention and transformers
Experience with entity resolution, fuzzy matching and deduplication across disparate third-party data sources
Experience with large language models, generative AI applications and prompt engineering for data classification, enrichment and analysis
Experience with MLOps, including scalable development to deployment of complex data science workflows
Experience with model explainability and interpretability techniques
Proficiency in Python and SQL required
Experience in machine learning frameworks and tools (e.g. scikit-learn, XGBoost, pandas, NumPy) required
Experience with ETL processes, data pipeline development and relational databases at scale
Experience with large-scale distributed computing and cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure or GCP
Experience with visualization platforms such as Tableau

Preferred

MBA, or PhD in a technical field
Background in consulting, professional services, or B2B analytics environments
Experience with pricing or profitability analytics in a B2B setting
Experience supporting deployment of SaaS or DaaS solutions with clients

The Role

US defense systems run on technical data that is often decades old: scanned paper, hand-marked prints, partial models, and drawings that were never turned into 3D models. A part that exists only on an old drawing is hard to source. That slows how fast the armed forces and our prime customers can sustain and rebuild the systems that use it. Hadrian turns that data into manufacturing-ready models and drawings, so customers can keep their systems running and Hadrian can make or procure the parts.

As a CAD Modeler, you build the 3D models and 2D drawings for naval and aerospace parts, starting from whatever the customer sends. You also build the models and drawings for each manufacturing state (M-state) of a part: the in-process configurations the factory builds and inventories on the way to the final part. Our engineers define each M-state, and you model, draw, and configure it. You own your parts from first model through release and every change after it.

Make the 2D drawings the factory runs on, from your models or the customer's.
Build the models and drawings for each M-state of a part.
Work out conflicting or unclear views against the rest of the drawing.
Keep PLM data correct and structured, and send your parts through the release workflow.

Build models that tooling, programming, and inspection teams can use as a base.
Work with manufacturing teams and turn around the model and drawing changes they need.

Experience building 3D models from complex 2D drawings with no existing model, including internal features that only show in a section view.

Experience releasing parts and controlling changes in a PLM system.

Production work in Siemens NX.

new_jobs.description:
Who We Are

Atoms is building the machines that power the next era of progress.

Over the last decade, software has transformed the digital world. But the physical world, where food is made, minerals are mined, goods are moved, and industries are run, remains far less intelligent, far less efficient, and far more constrained. We’re changing that.

Atoms builds Physical AI— real-world robots for the industries that move civilization forward, starting with food, mining, and transport. Our systems are designed to understand, predict, and control the real world with precision, turning complex physical operations into something more reliable, more scalable, and more productive.

This work requires more than robotics. It requires deep integration across hardware, software, AI, operations, manufacturing, and real estate. We don’t just build machines in a lab. We deploy them into real environments, operate them, learn from them, and improve them until they work at scale.

We are roboticists, engineers, operators, and builders. We believe the next great technology companies will not only transform information, but the physical systems that shape everyday life.

If you want to work on hard problems with real-world impact, join us.

About The Role

The QC Technician is the last check between our electronics and the field. You will flash firmware onto circuit boards every day, run functional tests, and make sure every board that leaves the bench is correctly programmed, traceable, and working.

This is a hands-on, bench-based role on the hardware production team. You will work closely with hardware and firmware engineers, follow documented procedures, and flag anything that looks off before it reaches a vehicle.

What You'll Do

Flash bootloaders, firmware, and configuration files onto PCBs and modules using programming fixtures, JTAG/SWD debuggers, USB/serial tools, and in-house scripts.
Confirm the correct firmware version and configuration is loaded on every board, matched to the build order, and run batch flashing efficiently while keeping error rates near zero.
Run functional and power-on tests after flashing, following test procedures and checklists; visually inspect boards for physical defects such as damaged components, solder issues, bent pins, and connector damage.
Use multimeters, power supplies, and basic test equipment to check voltages and continuity.
Separate passing and failing units, and tag failures clearly for engineering review. Write clear failure reports with symptoms, steps taken, and photos where useful.
Log serial numbers, firmware versions, test results, and failures in our tracking system or spreadsheets, label boards and keep inventory of programmed, tested, and failed units accurate.
Do first-level troubleshooting on failed flashes and tests: re-seat connections, check cables, retry, and swap fixtures–escalate recurring or unexplained failures to hardware and firmware engineers with enough detail to act on.
Follow ESD-safe handling and keep the bench, fixtures, and tools clean, calibrated, and organized, suggest improvements to procedures, fixtures, and scripts that cut cycle time or errors.
Help keep work instructions and checklists up to date as firmware and hardware change, and support new product introductions and engineering builds when needed.

High school diploma or equivalent; technical certificate or associate degree in electronics or a related field is a plus.
3+ year of hands-on experience in electronics manufacturing, test, QC, or a similar bench role.
Comfortable handling PCBs and small components with ESD-safe practices.
Basic use of a multimeter and bench power supply.
Comfortable on a linux computer: running programs or scripts from instructions, using a command line at an intermediate level, and entering data accurately in spreadsheets or tracking tools.
Able to follow written procedures exactly and recognize when something doesn't match them, clear written and verbal communication for logging results and reporting failures.
Reliable, consistent, and comfortable with repetitive, high-volume work.
Background in automotive, robotics, or heavy equipment electronics preferred.
IPC-A-610 or IPC J-STD-001 certification, or working knowledge of PCB workmanship standards preferred.
Experience flashing microcontrollers (STM32, ESP32, NXP, or similar) with tools such as ST-Link, J-Link, or OpenOCD preferred.
Familiarity with Linux and running Python or shell scripts preferred.
Experience with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, or serial terminals (UART, CAN), basic soldering and rework skills, and experience with test fixtures, bed-of-nails testers, or production test stations preferred.

Physical Requirements

Bench work in a lab or production environment, standing or seated for long periods.
Lift and move boxes and equipment up to 25 lb.
Close-up visual work with small components; magnification provided.
Use of ESD protective equipment required.

Why join us

At Atoms, you’ll work on one of the defining challenges of our time—bringing automation into the physical world to drive real, lasting impact. We exist to uncover valuable unknown truths and turn them into progress, which means constantly pushing beyond what’s known and building what doesn’t yet exist. The work is ambitious and often challenging, but it’s grounded in a shared sense of purpose and a team committed to seeing it through together. Our work only matters if it serves others, and we know that meaningful progress depends on the trust of the people we serve and the strength of our team—so we invest in both, creating an environment where you can do your best work and grow.

The Role

US defense systems run on technical data that is often decades old: scanned paper, hand-marked prints, partial models, and drawings that were never turned into 3D models. A part that exists only on an old drawing is hard to source. That slows how fast the armed forces and our prime customers can sustain and rebuild the systems that use it. Hadrian turns that data into manufacturing-ready models and drawings, so customers can keep their systems running and Hadrian can make or procure the parts.

As a CAD Modeler, you build the 3D models and 2D drawings for naval and aerospace parts, starting from whatever the customer sends. You also build the models and drawings for each manufacturing state (M-state) of a part: the in-process configurations the factory builds and inventories on the way to the final part. Our engineers define each M-state, and you model, draw, and configure it. You own your parts from first model through release and every change after it.

Build manufacturing-ready 3D models from naval prints, aerospace drawings, partial models, and other customer documents, matching the customer's definition feature for feature.
Make the 2D drawings the factory runs on, from your models or the customer's.
Build the models and drawings for each M-state of a part.
Work out conflicting or unclear views against the rest of the drawing.
Keep PLM data correct and structured, and send your parts through the release workflow.
Carry each customer change through the customer geometry and every related M-state across the part family.
Build models that tooling, programming, and inspection teams can use as a base.
Work with manufacturing teams and turn around the model and drawing changes they need.

Production work in Siemens NX.

Key Responsibilities

Interpret drawings and specifications, including tolerances, critical-to-quality dimensions (CTQs), surface finish requirements, material grades, and fit/function requirements.
Measure and verify product dimensions using tools such as calipers, micrometers, gauges, and plug gauges to confirm dimensional accuracy.
Follow established sampling rules, batch sampling plans, and acceptance limits to ensure pass/fail decisions are consistent and defensible, especially when 100% inspection is not practical.
Verify visual and finish standards, including surface defects, labeling, assembly correctness, weld/solder appearance (where applicable), and packaging integrity based on defined defect criteria.
Identify recurring quality issues and document trends. Support root-cause investigations using structured problem-solving tools such as Ishikawa (Fishbone) diagrams to analyze potential causes related to people, processes, materials, and equipment.
Initiate containment activities when necessary by holding suspect lots, isolating nonconforming material, and preventing the mixing of acceptable and questionable inventory.
Accurately record measurements, test results, and pass/fail decisions, including appropriate timestamps and batch or serial number identifiers.
Maintain traceability by linking inspection results to specific lot numbers, supplier batches, machine lines, and operator shifts when applicable.
Properly document deviations, including what failed, how it failed, and actions taken to address the issue.
Manage controlled documents and ensure the use of current checklists, SOPs, test methods, and inspection plans.
Support internal, customer, and regulatory audits by maintaining complete and accurate quality records.
Perform in-process inspections by verifying dimensions and process parameters at defined intervals throughout production.
Verify calibration status and condition of measuring tools, gauges, and inspection equipment, including calibration labels and due dates.
Validate mistake-proofing (Poka-Yoke) controls by ensuring sensors, fixtures, interlocks, and alarms function as intended and are not bypassed or ignored.

On an average 8-hour day, ability to walk, sit, stand, use hands to handle or feel, reach at or above shoulder height and below waist height, climb or balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; talk and hear, smell, and lift up to 50 pounds.

Operate pallet jack with a maximum weight load of 1,000 pounds during a scheduled shift as needed.
